title: Failed at Dieting Many Times: How to Start Again Differently This Time
intro: Failing at diets again and again is not a sign you're weak or lazy. Usually, the diet was too strict for your real life, so this time we start with a way you can keep up.

sections.p: Many diets cut out rice completely, ban all kuih, or have you eat too little. It might look like it's working in the first week, but it's hard to continue with work, family and eating out. When we slip, we feel like we've failed and stop completely.
Choose one or two changes you're confident you can do every day. For example, teh tarik kurang manis, or adding vegetables at lunch. Small but consistent works better than big but short-lived.

Weight can go up and down because of water, salt and your menstrual cycle. Also take your waist measurement, photos and notice how your clothes fit. A realistic target is around 0.5 to 1 kg a week, sometimes slower.
There will be functions, weekends and stressful days. That's normal. Instead of feeling like everything is ruined, just continue at your next meal. One meal doesn't cancel a week of effort.

Motivation is usually high in the first week and starts to drop in the second week. At this point, rely on routine, not motivation. Prepare packed meals, schedule your exercise and let your habits work for you.

action: Write down 2 small changes you're confident you can do every day this week.
Take your waist measurement and one photo today as your starting point.
Weigh yourself only once a week, on the same day and at the same time.
When you slip, continue again at your next meal, don't wait for Monday.
Schedule 2 short exercise sessions in your phone calendar.
myth: Many people think that once they've slipped, they have to wait until next Monday to start again. Actually you can just continue at your next meal, and that's the habit that helps the most.

faq.q: Do I need to count calories every day?
faq.a: Not compulsory. Some people like counting as a guide, others are more comfortable using a balanced plate. Calorie values are only estimates, so use them as a guide, not a strict rule.

faq.q: How long before I see results?
faq.a: Many people start noticing changes in their clothes and energy within 3-4 weeks. Clear changes in weight usually take longer. Keep going even if results are slow.

faq.q: I have PCOS or a thyroid problem, is this approach suitable?
faq.a: Basic habits like eating balanced meals, moving and getting enough sleep are usually good for many people. But every condition is different, so please get advice from your doctor for suitable guidance.
